result:
I fixed 12 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. I wrote a reference implementation from the docstrings and the module's common rules, then compared it with all 150 rules across about 260 quantities × 12 unit prices. After the fix, no rule differs from it.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 05, 87, 138, 140 | The cap only applied once the discount passed a higher amount (e.g. `if disc > 200000`), so discounts in between weren't capped | Always cap the discount |
| 16 | Discount used `round(... / 100)`, which can round up | Round down to the won (`// 100`) |
| 30 | Applied only above 100 (`qty > 100`), not at "100+" | Changed to `qty >= 100` |
| 118 | Threshold was 6 (`qty >= 6`), not 5 | Changed to `qty >= 5` |
| 135 | Threshold was 13 (`qty >= 13`), not 12 | Changed to `qty >= 12` |
| 45, 47 | Capped the price before applying the % | Calculate the discount first, then cap the discount |
| 134 | Capped the price above the threshold before applying the % | Calculate the discount first, then cap the discount |
| 86 | Docstring says "whole" but the code discounted only units above the threshold | Discount applies to the full amount (`base * 2 // 100`) |

The other 138 rules already matched their docstrings, so I left them alone. Negative-input handling (`_base`) and `RULES`/`quote` are unchanged.

STATUS: DONE
